statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is 5 of 100 in the low band, twenty points below the 25-point block threshold, because the CME weekend closure removes the price path this score measures. Stress is 57 in the elevated band on a still-shut Saudi East-West pipeline, WTI near $100.05, Houthi control of Yemen's Red Sea coast and a Wednesday policy decision priced near 85.6 percent for an increase. Confidence is 85 on a complete evidence set re-verified against primary sources this hour, with the shared cross-asset collector now outside its freshness window.
recommendation: Tail sits deep in the low band, so the deterministic mapping returns EA_ON and a green status, and the single shared reading applies to both NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. Two independent facts support it. First, Friday's completed path granted mean reversion rather than denying it: the Nasdaq-100 closed 29,368.44, up 264.93 points or 0.91%, yet finished about 105 points below its 29,473.12 high inside a 159.61-point cash range, while NQ futures traded down to 29,040.50 after the inflation print and recovered to settle 29,391.75, a round trip that retraced in both directions. Second, CME equity index futures halted at 21:00 UTC on Friday and do not reopen until 22:00 UTC on Sunday, sixteen hours after this horizon ends, so all twenty-four forecast slots describe a closed market in which a persistent no-retracement path cannot form. No evidence-based danger window is published, because a halted contract cannot define one. Stress remains elevated and is described here as an environment reading only: under the fixed repository mapping it does not alter the mapped state.
headline: A second full hour of a shut weekend tape with nothing changed: the Nasdaq-100 still shows its 29,368.44 close, VIX its 15.84, and the Saudi East-West pipeline outage, Houthi control of Yemen's Red Sea coast and Monday's Salalah meeting on Hormuz shipping all travel toward a Sunday reopen that falls beyond this window.
body:
This hour re-verified the full evidence set against primary sources and found nothing changed. The Nasdaq-100 quote page still shows a 29,368.44 close, up 264.93 points or 0.91%, inside a 29,313.51 to 29,473.12 range against a 29,103.51 previous close, so the cash range spanned only 159.61 points and the close finished about 105 points below the high. NQ futures were wider and more instructive: a 29,040.50 low after the 12:30 UTC inflation print gave way to a 29,499.50 high and a 29,391.75 settle, a round trip in which mean reversion worked in both directions. The broader tape agreed, with the Dow up 0.98% to 52,573.29, the S&P 500 up 0.86% to 7,656.98 and the Nasdaq Composite up 0.96% to 26,333.04, each snapping a losing streak while still finishing the week lower. VIX remains at 15.84, down 11.21%, having closed near the low of a 15.59 to 17.71 range.

The macro set behind that path is hawkish rather than disorderly. August CPI rose 0.4% on the month and 3.4% on the year, both matching expectations, with core at 0.3% on the month, one tenth above consensus. CME FedWatch put the probability of a 25 basis point increase at the 16 September FOMC at 85.6%, against 48.4% a month earlier, and Friday's live coverage reported roughly 87% by the close. Treasury yields are firm, with the H.15 series re-checked this hour showing the 2-year at 4.56%, the 5-year at 4.75%, the 10-year at 4.95% and the 30-year at 5.37% as of the 10 September observation. A firm but broadly in-line print that still allowed a 459-point round trip is evidence of orderly price discovery, which is why the event raises Stress and not Tail.

The unresolved risks remain in the Gulf and they are supply-route risks. Saudi Arabia's Energy Ministry shut the 7 million barrel per day East-West pipeline, the route that bypasses the Strait of Hormuz toward the Red Sea, after drone attacks in the Riyadh and Madinah regions that Riyadh attributed to launches from Iraqi territory. The Arab News report, updated 12 September at 00:21, still carries no restart date and only a statement that further developments will be announced. Houthi forces completed a rapid push to control Yemen's entire Red Sea coast on Friday, taking Mocha, Dhubab and the island of Perim, also called Mayyun, at the Bab al-Mandeb entrance. Against that, two things qualify the escalation: the Houthi military spokesman said maritime navigation is safe for all companies except Saudi vessels, and oil eased rather than extended, with WTI settling near $100.05, down 2.37%, and Brent near $104.61, down 2.81%, after Iran confirmed it will meet Gulf foreign ministers and Iraqi representatives in Salalah, Oman on Monday to discuss Hormuz shipping. A fresh check of the Al Jazeera live coverage and the Saudi reporting this hour found no new escalation and no retaliation announced.

One input degraded this hour rather than the picture itself. The shared cross-asset collector last refreshed at 05:11 UTC and now falls outside its 90-minute freshness window, so it is treated as stale background and not as support for any conclusion. Its calendar feed was already unavailable, so the calendar below rests on independently verified sources, re-checked this hour against the published United States economic calendar. What the stale file had shown remains consistent with the verified picture: Friday's advance was broad but internally dispersed, with seven of eight tracked megacaps higher on a mean gain near 0.94%, semiconductors uneven as ARM rose 4.17% and NVDA finished fractionally lower, and Treasury futures modestly lower in line with firm yields. Dispersion of that kind is the opposite of the single-direction alignment that precedes mean-reversion failure. Confidence therefore eases by one point to 85 rather than falling materially.

The decisive fact for this horizon stays mechanical. CME equity index futures halted at 21:00 UTC on Friday and reopen at 22:00 UTC on Sunday, sixteen hours after the last slot of this forecast. Every one of the twenty-four forward hours therefore describes a market in which no Nasdaq-100 price can print, so no persistent one-way path, no failed retracement and no session extreme can form. Conditional Tail is held at a low residual floor that steps from 5 to a 10 cap across the horizon, tracking accumulated unpriced weekend headline exposure ahead of an eventual reopen rather than any observed structure. No danger window is published, because a halted contract cannot define one.

lookbackSummary: All twenty-four clock-hours from 07:00 UTC on 11 September to 06:00 UTC on 12 September carry a published Claude assessment, so every lookback slot is available and none is reconstructed. The window opens in a trend-up read through the European hours, with Tail between 13 and 15 as the advance extended. The 12:30 UTC inflation print produced the only elevated readings of the window, Tail 21 and 22 in event/whipsaw mode with Confidence cut to 70 and then 80 while the post-release path was still forming. Tail fell back to 15 within ninety minutes as NQ retraced, held between 15 and 17 through the U.S. afternoon in mixed mode, then collapsed to 13 and 7 around the 21:00 UTC halt. The final nine slots sit at Tail 5 to 6 in normal mode, tracking the closure rather than a directional view, while Stress decayed steadily from 84 to 57 as the event passed and volatility fell.
outlookSummary: Every one of the twenty-four forward slots lies inside the CME weekend closure that began at 21:00 UTC on Friday, and the reference contract does not reopen until 22:00 UTC on Sunday, sixteen hours after this horizon ends. Conditional Tail opens at 5 in the current slot, the only slot containing observed rather than hypothetical structure, holds that residual floor for one more hour, then steps to 6, 7, 8 and 9 at roughly six-hour intervals before capping at 10 in the final three slots as unpriced weekend headline exposure accumulates ahead of an eventual reopen. Every slot stays deep in the low band, so the deterministic mapping returns EA_ON and green throughout. Stress runs 57 to a 61 ceiling and describes the environment rather than a path: a Saudi East-West pipeline outage whose latest update still carries no restart date, WTI near $100.05, Houthi control of Yemen's Red Sea coast qualified by a statement that navigation is safe except for Saudi vessels, Monday's Salalah meeting on Hormuz shipping and a Wednesday policy decision priced near 85.6 percent for an increase. Confidence decays from 85 to a 78 floor as the verified evidence set ages without any live price path to refresh it. No danger window is published, because a halted contract cannot define one.
